article.headline: Taylor Swift Returns to CMA Stage With Surprise Keith Urban Banjo Performance
article.summary: Taylor Swift marked her first CMA Awards performance in 13 years on November 18, 2026, by singing her Toy Story 5 track and a 2007 classic.
article.body:
Wearing a white-and-orange frock and cowgirl boots, Taylor Swift channeled the character Jessie from Toy Story for her live performance of "I Knew It, I Knew You" at the 60th Annual CMA Awards in Nashville. The set transformed into a nostalgic mash-up when Keith Urban joined her on the banjo for a rendition of her 2007 track "Our Song." This appearance marked Swift’s first time performing at the ceremony since 2013, when she performed "Red" alongside Vince Gill and Alison Krauss after receiving the Pinnacle Award.

For fans of the country music star, the performance highlights a conscious return to her musical origins. Swift, who last attended the event in 2016 to present the Entertainer of the Year honor to Garth Brooks, has recently spoken about feeling an increased loyalty to the people and the genre that shaped her career. The performance served as both a tribute to her country roots and a creative contribution to the Toy Story movie franchise, which she described as feeling like "coming home."

While her current single "I Knew It, I Knew You" earned a nomination for Single of the Year, the award ultimately went to Ella Langley for "Choosin' Texas." The 60th anniversary event was hosted by Lainey Wilson. Fans watching the ceremony had several digital options to follow the broadcast, including ABC and streaming platforms like Disney+, Hulu + Live TV, Fubo, and DirecTV.

article.headline: Taylor Swift returns to CMA stage with mashup after 13-year absence
article.summary: Taylor Swift performed at the 60th CMA Awards on Wednesday, marking her first time singing at the ceremony since 2013.
article.body:
Taylor Swift returned to the Country Music Association Awards stage on Wednesday night, performing a mashup that bridged her history with the genre. During her set, she sang "I Knew It, I Knew You"—a track featured in Disney and Pixar's "Toy Story 5"—and her first No. 1 country hit, "Our Song." Before beginning her performance, Swift acknowledged the lengthy break from the show, telling the audience, "It's been a while."

For country music fans and long-time followers of the awards, the performance signals a significant return for the artist, who last graced the CMA stage in 2013 to perform an acoustic version of "Red" with Alison Krauss and Vince Gill. Her presence at the 60th annual ceremony highlights her continued influence in the country music landscape, underscored by her nomination for Single of the Year for her contribution to the "Toy Story 5" soundtrack.

According to Good Morning America, Swift joined a lineup of performers for this year's 60th annual celebration, which featured artists including Ella Langley, Miranda Lambert, Kacey Musgraves, Cody Johnson, Tucker Wetmore, Tim McGraw, Zach Top, and The Red Clay Strays. The event was broadcast live on ABC and Disney+, with streaming availability beginning on Hulu the following day.

As Swift moves forward, her career remains a focal point of industry attention, both for her music and her recent life updates. The singer, who married Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce in July, continues to navigate her work across various entertainment sectors while retaining her roots in country music.

article.headline: Cowboys DT Quinnen Williams repeats six-word phrase twelve times to press corps
article.summary: Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle Quinnen Williams repeatedly dodged reporter questions ahead of the Week 11 matchup against the Philadelphia Eagles.
article.body:
Facing a barrage of inquiries from reporters, Quinnen Williams delivered a singular response throughout his entire media session: "I'm gonna keep that to myself." Williams opted to repeat this exact six-word refrain twelve times, regardless of the subject matter raised during the press conference leading up to the team's Week 11 clash with the Philadelphia Eagles. The interaction has sparked widespread speculation among NFL observers regarding the veteran defender's current mindset and his commitment to the organization.

The silence from Williams highlights a growing friction within a Cowboys locker room struggling through a difficult 4-6 season.
